body.statement: For constants whose bounds contain the displayed Jacobian ranges and for \(\beta\) below the displayed displacement and cut-locus margins, the construction in def:separable-witness satisfies \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\in\mathcal F_s\). The translation coordinates in the three triples returned by \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}\) are zero; the potential coordinates for \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}\) are respectively \(-0.1\cos(2\pi u_1)/(2\pi^2)\) and \(-0.15\cos(2\pi u_1)/(2\pi^2)+0.05\cos(2\pi u_2)/(2\pi^2)\). At \(u=(1/4,1/4)\) and \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\), its translation-aware displacement is \(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}(T,y)=(0.05/\pi,-0.05/\pi)\neq0\), its outer Jacobian is positive definite, and equal cell sizes give \(V_j=I_2/\pi\).
body.justification: The witness verifies nonemptiness, branch separation, nonzero displacement, and the candidate covariance at an analytic grid point.
body.gap: Its separability does not replace the requested nonseparable moving-pole analysis.
body.consumer: It supplies a reproducible benchmark for transport and adjoint solvers.
body.proof_tex:
The selected equivariant lifts in def:separable-witness have Jacobians
\[
Dh_0^{\mathrm{sep}}=I_2,qquad
Dh_1^{\mathrm{sep}}
=\operatorname{diag}(1+0.2\cos(2\pi u_1),1),
\tag{49}
\]
and
\[
Dh_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}
=\operatorname{diag}(1+0.3\cos(2\pi u_1),
1-0.1\cos(2\pi u_2)).
\tag{50}
\]
Their eigenvalues lie respectively in \([1,1]\), \([0.8,1.2]\), and \([0.7,1.3]\), so all three maps are orientation-preserving periodic diffeomorphisms.  Direct differentiation gives their mean-zero periodic potentials
\[
\phi_{h_1}(u)=-\frac{0.1}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_1),
\qquad
\phi_{h_{1\star}}(u)
=-\frac{0.15}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_1)
+\frac{0.05}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_2).
\tag{51}
\]
The average displacements of the three displayed lifts vanish, so their selected translation coordinates are zero.

Both latent laws are uniform and \(h_0^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the identity.  By lem:torus-cic-identification,
\[
p=h_1^{\mathrm{sep}},qquad
T=h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\circ(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}})^{-1}.
\tag{52}
\]
At \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\), the chain rule gives
\[
H(y)=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\frac{1+0.2\cos(2\pi u_1)}{1+0.3\cos(2\pi u_1)},
\frac1{1-0.1\cos(2\pi u_2)}
\right).
\tag{53}
\]
The two eigenvalue ranges are \([12/13,8/7]\) and \([10/11,10/9]\), hence \(H\) is uniformly positive definite.  Change of variables in the two pushforwards gives
\[
\frac56\leq f_{C1}\leq\frac54,
\qquad
\frac{100}{143}\leq f_{T1}\leq\frac{100}{63},
\qquad f_{C0}=f_{T0}=1.
\tag{54}
\]
All densities are smooth.  Thus ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, and ass:outer-ellipticity hold whenever the declared constants contain (49)--(54).

The two maps required by ass:cic-identification are \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and the map \(T\) in (52).  Their lifted Jacobians in (49) and (53) are symmetric positive definite, so their lifts are gradients of strictly convex functions.  The coordinate displacements of \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(T\) are bounded by \(0.1/\pi\) and \(0.05/\pi\), respectively, and hence remain strictly within the injectivity cell.  On this single squared-distance chart the convex dual inequality, summed around a finite cycle, proves \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclical monotonicity.  For \(T\), changing variables \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\) shows that each component of \(T(y)-y\) integrates to zero: it is a sine multiplied by products of constants and cosines.  Hence the selected translations of both \(p\) and \(T\) are zero.  Their distance from the boundary of \(\mathcal Q\) is \(1/2\), and their graphs have positive distance from \(\operatorname{Cut}_{\mathbb T}\).  Choosing \(\beta\) below these explicit margins proves ass:lift-regularity and therefore \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\in\mathcal F_s\).

At \(u=(1/4,1/4)\), all cosines in (53) vanish and
\[
y-T(y)
=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)-h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)
=\left(\frac{0.05}{\pi},-\frac{0.05}{\pi}\right)\neq0.
\tag{55}
\]
At the same point \(H(y)=I_2\), \(f_{T1}(y)=1\), and \(\alpha(y)=1\).  With equal cell-size ratios the definition of \(V(P)\) gives \(w_j=4\) and
\[
V_j=\frac{4I_2}{4\pi}=\frac{I_2}{\pi}.
\tag{56}
\]
This establishes every assertion of the proposition.
